_note: Boxes are NORMALISED to the tile (0-1). Contains a real WATERFALL (white 留白 stripes, not ink) and two collector seals that must never be treated as subject matter.

objects.name: big teal round-leaf tree spreading across the top left
objects.note: the dominant tree of the tile; leaf clusters clearly separated from pale ochre branches -- an ideal hinge subject. Canopy ONLY; its trunk is a separate object

objects.name: the dark trunk descending from that tree
objects.note: a trunk does NOT move; it is the anchor the canopy hinges above. Cataloguing it separately is what stops a colour gate fusing trunk into card

objects.name: waterfall dropping down the centre right
objects.note: three white 留白 stripes between dark rock edges -- there is NO ink to animate here, this is negative space and must be moved as water, not as strokes

objects.name: blue-green needle pine on the right ledge
objects.note: flat needle fans on ochre branches; sprays hang off a nearly horizontal limb, so swing reads strongly here

objects.name: rust dot-cluster tree at the right edge
objects.note: clipped; continues into the tile to the right

objects.name: cliff wall down the whole left edge
pale cliff face behind the trunk
objects.note: the flattest passage in the tile; a good clean-plate donor

objects.name: rock ledge the pine stands on
objects.note: the pine's roots grip this -- share its depth plane

objects.name: two red collector seals on the cliff
objects.note: vermilion seal impressions sit ON the silk, not IN the scene. They must never enter a card, a plane, or a colour gate -- red is exactly what a maple gate looks for
